goals.title: A bird who can't fly builds its own wings
goals.critique: After five treadwheel rounds this is finally a new direction, and the strongest pitch so far. The build, jump, crash, rebuild loop gives a reason to try again every minute, every crash has a cause you can read in the wing you built, and 'three metres short' is a clip people send. But a flightless bird launching itself again and again towards a distance mark is the premise of Learn to Fly, and part-built flyers are Besiege and Kerbal ground, so it caps near 6 unless the materials make it Lumi's own. The progress also runs on one axis, distance, and once the far island is reached nothing pulls the player back. The physics is fragile in the same way the arch was: a vortex-lattice wing with a swinging body under it, weight-shift steering and wet paper sagging (which quietly needs a deforming structure) all have to be stable and honest, or the 'fails for a reason you can see' promise turns into noise, and fudged lift is exactly the shortcut that would make the payoff a lie.
